messages:
maria: Quick Q — we're about to land a TF change that adds a KMS grant scoped to a namespaced IAM role (IRSA). My worry: helm releases (esp. external-secrets & cert-manager) sometimes create ServiceAccount then immediately mount/secrets and try to decrypt before the KMS grant or annotation propagates. Could this make our rollout fail? pinging @ryan for infra ordering advice :thinking:

maria: Here's the terraform snippet we're applying (simplified):
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "svcacct_decrypt" {
  name        = "svcacct-decrypt-${var.namespace}"
  key_id      = aws_kms_key.app_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn
  operations  = ["Decrypt"]
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "irsa_role" {
  # role created with oidc principal for namespace
}
```

ryan: Short answer: yes, if the pod starts before the grant is active you’ll see DecryptDenied errors. In practice two things matter: TF apply order & AWS eventual consistency for KMS grants. If helm creates SA and pods fast, external-secrets/controller can race.

ryan: Mitigations:
- Ensure TF creates the KMS grant before workloads are rolled (apply earlier or run a separate staging apply).
- Add an explicit `depends_on` where possible (e.g., helm_release resource depends_on aws_kms_grant).
- Add a tiny readiness check to controllers that need decrypt (or post-install job that retries decrypt).

jess: We hit this with the vectorizer secret last month. We added a little post-install job in the chart that sleeps + runs `kubectl rollout restart` for the deployment that reads the secret. Ugly but effective. :grimacing:

sam: Another pattern: have the chart create SA first, but don't create the secret consumer (or scale the consumer to 0) until after we trigger a separate job that confirms KMS grant exists. Could also use an initContainer that retries Decrypt on startup and fails open/backoff.

maria: Good tips. Is `depends_on` supported for our helm_release in the TF module? I think helm provider supports depends_on at the resource level. Would that block the release until grant is visible everywhere?

ryan: Yes you can do: `resource "helm_release" "app" { depends_on = [aws_kms_grant.svcacct_decrypt] ... }`. That makes terraform wait until grant creation call returns. It doesn't fully guarantee AWS global propagation but reduces race surface. Also after grant creation, KMS policies sometimes take ~1-2s to be usable, but could be more in cross-account scenarios.

maria: Good to know. Our KMS key is in the same account. Also we use a namespaced role with OIDC trust. Cross-account not involved.

jess: If you want minimal blast radius, add a small `local-exec` null_resource that polls `aws kms list-grants --key-id <id>` until the grantee principal appears, then let helm run. That gives a stronger signal than tf success alone.

maria: (sharing quick poll script idea)
```bash
# wait for grant to appear
for i in {1..30}; do
  aws kms list-grants --key-id $KEY | grep -q $GRANTEE && break
  sleep 2
done
```

sam: ^ this is what we used for the cert-manager rollout. Works reliably.

infra-bot: CI:terraform-plan #782 succeeded for branch/feat/kms-irsa (plan shows aws_kms_grant added).

maria: Ok plan is green. I'll:
- add `depends_on` to the chart helm_release in our infra repo,
- add a null_resource poller that ensures the KMS grant is visible,
- and include a small postInstall hook in the chart that restarts the consumers if they fail first time.

maria: @ryan @jess @sam can you review the PR when I open it? I'll link the branch here. :pray:

ryan: Happy to review. If you can keep the poller script in the infra repo (not chart), even better — avoids chart logic changes.

jess: +1. I'll look at the postInstall hook to make sure it doesn't break upgrades.

sam: lgtm, ping me if you want me to run the apply in staging.

maria: Thanks all — PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/pull/1423 (includes depends_on + poller + helm hook). I'll run staged apply tomorrow morning and let the team know results. :rocket:
